overview: Register (July-Sept 1941) traces Japan's English-language telephone ban, State's authorized protest despite Grew's futility warning, Japan's rejected British-precedent justification, U.S. insistence on diplomatic necessity, and the September 13 restoration of foreign-language calls.

subfiles.title: List of papers on Japanese telephone laws and regulations
subfiles.about: A two-page file register summarizes diplomatic correspondence about Japan’s 1941 prohibition and subsequent restoration of foreign-language telephone communications.
subfiles.summary: Register traces Japan's 1941 ban on English telephone calls, State's authorized protest despite Grew's doubts, Japan's rejected claim of British precedent, and the September 19 report that foreign-language calls resumed September 13.

interest: Tracks the 1941 U.S.-Japan telephone-language dispute from protest through resolution, with Britain's precedent rejected.
